t.1.15.1: At that very time, O you whose wealth is austerity, those two sisters saw Uccaiḥśravas approaching close by.
t.1.15.2: It was that peerless jewel among horses, born while the amṛta was being churned, whom all the hosts of the gods honored with delight.
t.1.15.4: Śaunaka said: Tell me how and where that amṛta was churned by the gods, there where that mighty and greatly radiant king of horses was born.
t.1.15.3: That best of horses, foremost among the swift, possessed of the strength of a mighty flood, glorious, unaging, divine, and marked with every auspicious sign.
t.1.15.5: They went to Meru, the blazing mountain, an unsurpassed mass of splendor, which casts back the radiance of the sun with its own peaks shining with gold.
t.1.15.7: That great mountain, frequented by fearsome serpents and lit up by celestial herbs, stood covering the vault of heaven with its height.
t.1.15.6: Adorned with golden ornaments, wondrous, frequented by gods and Gandharvas, immeasurable, and unassailable by people steeped in adharma.
t.1.15.8: That mountain, which others cannot reach even in thought, is rich in rivers and trees and echoes with the calls of flocks of many kinds of most charming birds.
t.1.15.10: Seated there, the dwellers of heaven, steadfast in austerity and self-restraint, came together and began to take counsel for the sake of the amṛta.
t.1.15.11: While the gods were thus pondering and taking counsel together on every side, the god Nārāyaṇa then spoke these words to Brahmā.
t.1.15.9: All the gods of great might, having climbed onto its beautiful back, studded with many jewels, onto that soaring height that seemed almost without end,
t.1.15.12: Let the pitcher-like ocean be churned by the gods and the hosts of Asuras; when the great ocean is being churned, the amṛta will arise there.
t.1.15.13: Having cast in all the herbs and all the jewels as well, churn the ocean, O gods; then you will obtain the amṛta.
